subject: Send Exit Utilization before Enter to prevent conflict

comments.message:
Patch Set 1: Ok-To-Test+1

User approved, CI ok to start

Patch Set 1: Verified+1

Build Successful 

https://jenkins.openbmc.org/job/ci-repository/129002/console : SUCCESS
Haven't you now just caused the same bug in reverse?

No, because when the app finds this condition is will always replace the enter util with the exit util. Here are examples of original, fix, and reverse:

Original code example:
  initial utils: enter = 8, exit = 12
  user requests: enter = 18, exit = 22
  app gets exit value first and sees that (new enter) 18 > (current exit) 12, so it updates both to the current exit value (12)
  app then gets exit value and updates the exit to 22
  BAD resulting values: enter = 12, exit = 22

With fix:
  initial utils: enter = 8, exit = 12
  user requests: enter = 18, exit = 22
  app gets exit value first and updates it -> enter = 8 and exit = 22
  app then gets enter value and updates the enter to 18
  GOOD resulting values: enter = 18, exit = 22

Reverse case with fix:
  initial utils: enter = 8, exit = 12
  user requests: enter = 4, exit = 6
  app gets exit value first and sees that (current enter) 8 > (new exit) 6, so it updates both to the new exit value (6)
  app then gets enter value and updates the enter to 4
  GOOD resulting values: enter = 4, exit = 6

> app gets exit value first and sees that (new enter) 18 > (current exit) 12, so it updates both to the current exit value (12)

Isn't this a bug?  Why wouldn't it set both enter and exit to the new value?  (Ie, one value bumps, the other value bumps automatically so that it's always valid).  How does this work if you PATCH only one parameter?


If we're relying on the order of dbus requests and it's required, I suspect there's something broken in our API definition.  Technically there's nothing in this code that guarantees the order (although it is very...very likely).

If we can't do the above, and we have constraints on set order, I suspect the property set interface isn't really what we should be using here, because technically the property API sets no constraint on order.

Overall, I'd really like to see a solution that resolves this in the backend.   Randomly rearranging working code doesn't guarantee that someone won't immediately rearrange it back, and if there are multiple backends for this per-cpu interface, I'm worried we're going to impose silent constraints on this.

Patching only one parameter is fine because the user should know that enter must be less than or equal to the exit.

The order of the setDbusProperty requests is sequential in this function, why are you saying it is not guaranteed?

The dbus SET can only set one property at a time, which is the root problem with this situation.

Another option would be for the app to wait some period of time (for any new dbus requests before doing the checking), but I really think that is a must less desirable solution because of the time dependency (how long do you wait, etc).

> Patching only one parameter is fine because the user should know that enter must be less than or equal to the exit.

Should they?

> 
> The order of the setDbusProperty requests is sequential in this function, why are you saying it is not guaranteed?
> 
> The dbus SET can only set one property at a time, which is the root problem with this situation.

Right.

> 
> Another option would be for the app to wait some period of time (for any new dbus requests before doing the checking), but I really think that is a must less desirable solution because of the time dependency (how long do you wait, etc).

Other options:
1. A method call that lets us set both at once
2. Make max push min, and min push max.  Ie, if you PATCH max < min, min is changed to match max to keep everything valid.  We did this in IPMI somewhere else in the past and it worked well for customers.  There are customers that patch each value independently with reckless disregard for ordering.
